subject: Approval request: Senior Runtime Engineer offer — comp band exception & vesting
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sr Runtime - comp band exception request / vesting schedule ask

Ava,

Following up from last week's calibration: we've found a strong candidate for the Senior Runtime Engineer role (Alex Singh). Quick summary: strong systems background, shipped a production KV cache for a serving runtime, and familiarity with low-level GPU kernel tuning. Recruiter attached resume and comp exception request.

Ask: I want to extend an offer but need a one-step exception to the published comp band for Senior (Band 4 -> request Band 4+). The specific asks are:
- Base: $195k (market ask $200k, band mid is $170k)
- RSU: 0.45% 4yr vesting with 12-month cliff + proposed 18-month acceleration on change-in-control clause
- Signing bonus: $20k

Rationale: immediate impact on runtime perf initiatives (K/V cache and compilation optimizations), candidate would lead a small infra optimization pod which directly reduces per-token cost. Hiring manager (me) is comfortable with the upside.

Can you please advise:
1) Is the comp exception approvable from compensation/finance perspective?
2) Any guidance on the change-in-control vesting acceleration — is 18 months likely to be flagged?
3) If approved, can Ben route this for procurement and exec signoff?

Attachments: Alex_Singh_Resume.pdf, comp_band_exception_request.xlsx

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sr Runtime - comp band exception request / vesting schedule ask

Marissa —

Thanks, this is clear and the case is compelling. A few notes after quick calibration with comp ops:
- Base: $195k is OK as an exception to Band 4 provided we document candidate scarcity and direct revenue/cost impact. Please fill the spreadsheet tab 'scarcity_impact' with metric-backed KPIs (expected latency % improvement, cost-per-request reduction estimate).
- RSU 0.45%: that pushes slightly above the typical midpoint for Senior; comp ops requests we reduce to 0.35% unless hiring manager signs off on measurable instrumentation metrics tied to the role in first 6 months. If you want 0.45%, we'll need an SVP approval note.
- 18-month change-in-control acceleration: this is non-standard. Standard is 12-month acceleration or milestone-based acceleration (e.g., successful rollout of K/V cache to production by month 12). Finance is okay with milestone-based language.
- Signing bonus $20k is fine.

Processwise: I'll flag this to compensation review (we aim for a 48-hour turnaround) and Kimberly — please confirm budget headcount alignment for Q4 tranche. Ben, if comp ops signs off, can you prepare the offer packet + DocuSign and coordinate with procurement for the candidate background check/contracting SR?

I attached a suggested offer language snippet for vesting/acceleration you can reuse. Also cc'd Priyom for offer-band notes so recruiting can align the candidate expectations.

Best,

Ava Chen
Senior Manager, Talent Partnerships (Acting for Offer Ops)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: suggested_vesting_snippet.txt (see offer language)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sr Runtime - comp band exception request / vesting schedule ask

Ava/Marissa —

Quick read: I'm okay to proceed to offer issuance once comp ops returns formal sign-off. Procurement will need the finalized offer packet (PDF) and candidate info to kick off background and payroll set-up. Please include the HubSpot deal ID and candidate email in the packet (I'm attaching the template we use).

I will not sign the exception myself for RSUs >0.4%; that requires VP-level approval. If you want to keep the 0.45% ask, Marissa, please prepare a one-page business case for VP review outlining: 1) incremental annualized cost, 2) expected month-over-month unit-cost improvement, and 3) expected time-to-production.

Small admin ask: route the final offer packet to procurement@redwood.example.com and cc me. I can route for expedited signoff if the business case is strong.

Ben Carter
Head of People Ops (Comp & Procurement)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: procurement_offer_template.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Alex Singh <alex.singh@example.com>, Erin Lopez <recruiter@talent-hub.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sr Runtime - comp band exception request / vesting schedule ask

Folks —

Following the notes above, comp ops approved the Band 4 exception with conditions: base $195k, RSU 0.35% baseline with a 0.10% performance tranche that vests on meeting production KPIs at month 12 (detailed in the packet). Vesting acceleration will be milestone-based (production deployment milestone at month 12 triggers acceleration language).

Ben — I've attached the final approved-offer-packet.pdf and the completed 'scarcity_impact' tab with KPI estimates (latency -18% on targeted 99th p95 path, estimated $0.0008/token reduction). Please start procurement flow and prepare DocuSign.

Alex/Erin — pending official DocuSign, we're aiming to send the offer this afternoon PST. Welcome aboard (conditional on standard checks).

Thanks all —

Marissa Cole
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
